To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the antenna gain decreases and the return loss increases as the thickness of the concrete cover and the air-gap between the antenna and the concrete increase.

(a) the gain of the embedded patch antenna is significantly reduced as the air-gap thickness is reduced, (b) the gain of an embedded patch antenna is reduced with increase in the concrete cover thickness, (c) the return loss properties are not significantly affected with change in the air-gap or concrete thickness.
the gain and transmission loss are both functions of the air gap and concrete cover thickness and that wireless power transmission to embedded antennas in concrete is possible.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of an embedded antenna for structural health applications and the characterization of gain and return loss of such an antenna as a function of the airgap and the concrete cover thickness.
the gain and return-loss properties of embedded microstrip patch antennas and their potential use in wireless power transmission for structural health monitoring applications.
the gain and return losses of an embedded micro-strip patch antenna in a concrete environment, and the wireless power transmission between two such antennas.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a microstrip patch antenna can be embedded within concrete and can be used for wireless communication as well as for wireless power transmission.
the gain and return-loss of the embedded antenna can be controlled to a large extent by the air-gap and the concrete cover thickness.
the embedded microstrip patch antennas can be used for structural health monitoring applications with the help of the proposed wireless power transmission scheme.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the embedded patch antenna is suitable for structural health monitoring applications.
embedded antennas can be used in wireless power transmission and data communication applications for structural health monitoring.

the gain and transmission properties of the embedded microstrip patch antennas are significantly degraded by the concrete, but can be improved by increasing the air-gap and reducing the concrete cover.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the antenna embedded within concrete can be used for wireless communication and power transfer.
the embedded antenna can be made to operate at a resonant frequency that is not affected significantly by the concrete cover thickness.
a small air-gap is needed for good performance of embedded antennas.
